title: Bounds, supremum, infimum, and order completeness
section: Real Analysis ▷ The Completeness of the Real Numbers
terms: upper bound; lower bound; bounded above; bounded below; least upper bound; supre- mum; greatest lower bound; infimum; least upper bound axiom.

exposition.text:
An upper bound u for A ⊆ R satisfies a ≤ u for every a ∈ A. The supremum is the least upper
bound; the infimum is the greatest lower bound. A maximum or minimum must belong to the
set, whereas a supremum or infimum need not.
Every nonempty real set bounded above has a finite real supremum, and the dual statement
holds below. The nonempty hypothesis matters. If s = sup A, then every ε > 0 admits a ∈ A
with s − ε < a ≤ s. Rational numbers lack this completeness: rational sets can have irrational
real suprema.
A lower bound ℓ satisfies ℓ ≤ a for every a ∈ A; bounded below means that at least one such
real ℓ exists. The empty set is bounded above and below vacuously but has no real supremum
or infimum, since every real number is a bound and none is least or greatest as appropriate. An
unattained finite supremum can always be approached by a strictly increasing sequence from
the set.

solution.text:
Even indices give 1 + 1/n, maximized at n = 2 with value 3/2. Odd indices give −1 + 1/n >
−1 and approach −1, so the infimum is −1 but is not attained.

question.text:
Nonempty bounded subsets A, B ⊂ R satisfy sup A = 3, inf A = −1, sup B = 4, and inf B = 2.
What is sup{a − b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B}?
(A) −5 (B) −1 (C) 1 (D) 2 (E) 7

solution.text:
Every difference is at most 3 − 2 = 1. Given ε > 0, choose a > 3 − ε/2 and b < 2 + ε/2 using
the definitions of supremum and infimum. Then a − b > 1 − ε, proving the supremum is 1.

question.text:
If A ⊂ (0, ∞) has inf A = 2 and sup A = 5, what is sup{1/a : a ∈ A}?
(A) 5
(B) 2
(C) 1/5
(D) It depends on whether 2 ∈ A
(E) 1/2

solution.text:
Reciprocation reverses order on positive numbers. The reciprocal values are bounded
above by 1/2 and approach it as elements of A approach their infimum; attainment is
unnecessary.
